data.turoyo: W koḥəškile ʕal ḥḏoḏe, yaʕni mdawsile ġalabe ʕal ḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: und drückt ihn fest zusammen, d. h. stampft ihn fest zusammen.

rationale: Second Infectum context; compacting a mass ʕal ḥḏoḏe contrasts with tobacco packed into a pipe, retaining the same core meaning.

summary: The plural processing agents and indexed mass object instantiate ordinary I Infectum; no new stem or Detransitive form.
The ʕal ḥḏoḏe expression presents material pressed together; mdawsile intensifies/explicates the action in the same verse. Do not derive a separate trampling sense for ḥšk from the paraphrase.
The reader identifies the mass as chaff, but the supplied verse contains only -le/ihn. Preserve the edition's anaphoric text rather than inventing a Turoyo noun or a new translation.
Recover the material antecedent of -le from the edition if an independently understandable expanded quotation is wanted; the supplied one-line verse does not itself name the chaff.
Is container-free compression productive, or specialized to this processing context? Both current examples fit broad stopfen.
